"Built on modern semiconductor processes, the S1 can be produced at a scale and price-point that is perfect for consumer wearables." → deployment_awareness_absence / operator_absence (entirely consumer-market framing, zero mention of DDIL/ATO/RMF/CMMC/ITAR/operators despite an active AF award)

blind_spots.blind_spot: S1 sensor is marketed as 'contact free' for weather/sweat/sleeve-proof consumer wearables, with no mention of gloves, helmets, or combat gear obstructing sensor placement.
blind_spots.operator_reality: An operator in full PPE at an austere site has hands and head covered by tactical gear; the biomagnetic sensor needs proximity to specific body sites the gear will block — not addressed anywhere in their materials.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Product was designed for consumer health/HCI wearables market; the AF award appears to be a narrow research add-on to that core roadmap.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The S1 operates without the need for direct contact to the skin, making it easy to integrate into wearables that need to be weather, sweat and sleeve-proof for people on the go.

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Low power & cost' framing is scoped entirely to consumer-wearable mass production economics, with no mention of ruggedization, MIL-STD environmental testing, or field battery/spares logistics.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Sustained field deployment requires battery replacement and spares logistics in DDIL conditions; consumer low-power framing doesn't address ruggedization for dust, shock, or temperature extremes.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The company's entire public roadmap (Early Access Program, consumer signup form) targets a civilian product launch, not a fielded military unit.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Built on modern semiconductor processes, the S1 can be produced at a scale and price-point that is perfect for consumer wearables.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No mention of ATO/RMF or controlled-data handling for biometric/neural telemetry, despite marketing the platform's ability to capture 'thoughts' data and holding an active Air Force Human-Machine Teaming award.
blind_spots.operator_reality: Collecting and transmitting neural/biometric data from operators on a DoD network requires an Authority to Operate and likely CMMC/ITAR review before any fielded use — none evidenced despite the funded program.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team is composed of neuroscience/semiconductor researchers and consumer-product operators, not deployment or compliance engineers.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: capturing the clearest picture yet of our bodies, health, feelings, and even our thoughts.

opener_hook: Sonera's $1.25M Air Force Phase II funds a biomagnetic sensor for Human-Machine Teaming — every public spec on the underlying S1 chip is optimized for consumer wearables instead.
what_they_do: Makes chip-scale contactless biomagnetic sensors for consumer neural/muscle-activity wearables, with a separate Air Force-funded human-machine-teaming variant.
